fact: The Central African Republic's and the DRC's digital ministers, meeting in Moscow on 8 October 2026, agreed on the need to carry out the CAR-DRC fibre-optic interconnection to reach the Moanda cable landing, with no timetable or financing agreement announced.

Africa50 and Bayobab (MTN GlobalConnect) announced a partnership in May 2023 to develop Project East2West, a US$320-325 million terrestrial fibre network linking landlocked countries to coastal cables, with the DRC among the twelve countries the document names as covered (planned end year 2026); the DRC government is not named as a party.

Tech Africa News reports that in February 2026 Paratus activated a 2,000-kilometre protected fibre route linking Mombasa to Goma via Nairobi, Kampala and Kigali, giving eastern DRC direct high-capacity access to subsea systems on the Kenyan coast; the document states capacity available and no traffic figures or named buyer.

Paratus said at the ITW and Datacloud Africa Conference that its 2,000 km Goma-to-Mombasa terrestrial fibre route, linking eastern DRC to Kenya via Kigali, Kampala and Nairobi, is live and carrying traffic.

Tanzania's foreign minister reaffirmed, in a meeting with the DRC ambassador, that the two countries are pursuing construction of a fibre-optic cable from Kigoma in Tanzania to Kalemie in DRC across Lake Tanganyika and agreed to fast-track it; no date of original agreement, contract, cost or works start is given.

fact: Paratus (press release republished by ITWeb Africa) said it switched on its 2,000 km Goma-to-Mombasa protected terrestrial fibre route via Kigali, Kampala and Nairobi, already carrying traffic for its first wholesale customers, with partners ROKE TELKOM in Uganda and MoveOn Telecoms in Kenya.

The DRC-Burundi fibre-optic interconnection project, a joint initiative between the two countries, had its memorandum of understanding adopted by Burundi's Council of Ministers on 8 May 2024, per ABP.
